fieldValues.title: ProtocolSummary carried no targetType, so nothing could find a Protocol by what it governs
fieldValues.summary: The service's ProtocolSummary omitted targetType — the one field that says what a Protocol is for. Adding it to the summary is additive and flows straight through to the CLI's srs protocol list payload as well as the MCP list resource, so a client filters by target type without a second call.
evidence: targetType is newly carried by ProtocolSummary and therefore by srs protocol list; the payload golden was regenerated
A protocol_find_by_target_type tool exists in the service but was not exposed: the list resource carries targetType, so an agent filters client-side
Before this, a Protocol was reachable over MCP only through a Blueprint prompt whose first rootTypes entry matched its targetType
fieldValues.body: The general shape worth carrying: when a summary type omits the field that answers the question the summary exists for, consumers route around it — here, through an unrelated Blueprint prompt whose match was incidental. Adding the field to the shared summary was cheaper than adding a finder verb, and it kept the CLI and MCP surfaces identical, which is what capability layering is for. An additive field on a summary struct regenerates the payload golden but breaks no consumer.
